question: 专业人士能因信念拒绝服务吗？
question_en: May a professional refuse to serve on grounds of conscience?
sub: 同一条良心自由，换个人来用，我们怎么就不认了？
sub_en: Why does the same freedom of conscience stop looking right when someone else invokes it?

casting.reason: 他在沃尔姆斯拒绝撤回著作，是西方『良心不可强迫』最著名的一幕。他第一个开口，站在最硬的一端：职业义务压不过良心，连转介也算参与。
casting.reason_en: His refusal to recant at Worms is the West's most famous scene of a conscience that will not be coerced. He speaks first and holds the hardest line: no professional duty outranks conscience, and even a referral counts as taking part.

casting.reason: 他把私人良心看作国家的病根，主张法律才是公共的良心；但他也写过士兵找人顶替就可拒绝。他给出的方案是：你可以不做，但得先把接手的人安排好。
casting.reason_en: He sees private conscience as a disease of the commonwealth and holds that the law is the public conscience, yet he also wrote that a soldier may refuse if he supplies a substitute. His answer: you may decline, but only after arranging who takes over.

casting.reason: 他论证过『违背良心总是恶，哪怕良心错了』，同时坚持良心须受教育。他把拒绝做某个行为与拒绝服务某种人严格分开，并指出隐瞒病人的出路是另一桩过错。
casting.reason_en: He argued that acting against conscience is always wrong even when conscience errs, while insisting that conscience must be formed. He separates refusing an act from refusing a kind of person, and points out that hiding a patient's alternatives is a second wrong.

casting.reason: 《论宗教宽容》的作者，主张信仰不受强制，但对人人适用的法律若与良心冲突，人可以不做、须自己承受惩罚。他的判据是：拒绝的成本落在谁身上。
casting.reason_en: The author of A Letter Concerning Toleration holds that belief must not be coerced, but when a general law clashes with conscience one may abstain and must bear the penalty oneself. His test: on whom does the cost of refusal fall?

casting.reason: 他为不服从不义之法辩护，又亲历过午餐柜台以『信念』拒绝黑人。他提出全场最关键的一条线：良心拒绝一件事，和良心拒绝一种人，是两样东西。
casting.reason_en: He defended disobedience to unjust laws, and he also lived through lunch counters refusing Black customers in the name of 'conviction.' He draws the debate's pivotal line: refusing a deed on conscience is one thing, refusing a kind of person is another.

casting.reason: 他亲赴楚国劝阻公输盘造攻城器械，是最早为工匠的道义发言的人。他以兼爱为尺：可以推掉一件活，不可以挑人服务，判断标准是百姓得不得利。
casting.reason_en: He traveled to Chu to stop Gongshu Ban from building siege engines, one of the first voices on a craftsman's ethics. His measure is impartial care: you may turn down a job but not pick whom to serve, and the test is whether the people benefit.

casting.reason: 他认为竞争市场会让歧视者自己付出代价，并批评执照制度人为压低供给。他把问题重新框定：拒绝之所以伤人，往往是因为只剩一家。
casting.reason_en: He holds that competitive markets make discriminators pay for their choices and criticizes licensing for keeping supply artificially low. He reframes the problem: refusal hurts mostly because there's only one provider left.

casting.reason: 道德心理学家，研究直觉如何先于理由。他指出我们对良心拒绝的判断常随立场翻转，提出『互换测试』，并揭穿『拒绝事不拒绝人』这条线也可被描述操纵。
casting.reason_en: A moral psychologist who studies how intuition runs ahead of reasons. He shows that our verdicts on conscientious refusal flip with our politics, proposes a swap test, and exposes how even 'refuse the deed, not the person' can be gamed through description.

casting.reason: 她写过专书梳理美国的良心自由传统，主张少数人的良心须受平等尊重；又以能力进路为底线：豁免不能让病人跌到基本能力门槛以下。她给出全场最可操作的判据：可替代与否、紧急与否。
casting.reason_en: She wrote a book on America's tradition of liberty of conscience and holds that minority consciences deserve equal respect, while using the capabilities approach as a floor: no exemption may push a patient below a basic threshold. Her standard is the most usable in the debate: is there an alternative, and is it urgent?

posts.text: 1521年在沃尔姆斯，皇帝和教会要我撤回著作。我答：我的良心被上帝的话语俘虏，违背良心既不正确，也不安全。**一个人若能被一纸职业要求逼着去做他认定是恶的事，他就不再是人，只是一件工具。**医生、药剂师先是人，执照是后来才有的。你可以开除我、罚我，但命令不了我的良心。
posts.text_en: At Worms in 1521, the emperor and the church demanded that I recant my writings. I answered that my conscience was captive to the Word of God, and that to go against conscience is neither right nor safe. **A person who can be forced by a job description to do what he judges evil is no longer a person, only a tool.** A doctor or a pharmacist is a human being first; the license came later. You may fire me or fine me, but you cannot command my conscience.

glossary.沃尔姆斯: Diet of Worms（沃尔姆斯帝国议会）：1521年神圣罗马帝国在沃尔姆斯召开的会议。路德在皇帝面前拒绝撤回著作，随后被宣布为法外之人。

glossary_en.Worms: The Diet of Worms, the imperial assembly of 1521 where Luther refused before the emperor to recant his writings and was afterwards declared an outlaw.

posts.text: 路德先生，你那一套后来让欧洲打了上百年的宗教战争。人人以私人良心为法官，正是国家的病根。**法律就是公共的良心。**但我不要谁去当殉道者。我写过：被征召的士兵若胆怯，找一个合格的人顶替自己，就可以拒绝而不算不义。放到医院也一样：你可以不做，前提是病人到你面前之前，你已经把替你做的人安排好。
posts.text_en: Herr Luther, your way of thinking went on to give Europe more than a century of religious war. When every man makes his private conscience his judge, the commonwealth is sick at the root. **The law is the public conscience.** But I want no one to be a martyr. I wrote that a man pressed as a soldier who is fearful may refuse without injustice if he puts an able soldier in his place. A hospital is no different: you may decline, provided that before the patient reaches you, you have already arranged who will do it instead.

glossary.公共的良心: public conscience（公共的良心）：霍布斯《利维坦》第29章语。私人良心只是个人意见；在国家之中，法律才是人们已经同意受其引导的『公共良心』。

glossary_en.public conscience: Hobbes, Leviathan ch. 29: private conscience is only private opinion; within a commonwealth the law is the public conscience that subjects have already agreed to be guided by.

posts.text: 先立反方：良心会错，错的良心还算数吗？我的回答是：**违背良心行事总是恶，哪怕那良心本身错了。**所以不可逼医生亲手做他确信是杀人的事。但这不等于他可以挑病人。拒绝做某个行为，和拒绝服务某种人，是两回事：前者关乎行为本身的善恶，后者往往只是厌恶。再者，良心有受教育的义务，没想清楚的感觉不能冒充良心。
posts.text_en: Let me state the objection first: conscience can err, so does an erroneous conscience still count? My answer: **to act against conscience is always evil, even when that conscience is itself mistaken.** So no doctor should be forced to do with his own hands what he is convinced is killing. But that does not let him choose his patients. Refusing an act and refusing a kind of person are two different things: the first concerns the goodness of the act itself, the second is usually mere aversion. And conscience has a duty to be formed; an unexamined feeling may not pass itself off as conscience.

glossary.错的良心: erroneous conscience（错误的良心）：阿奎那《神学大全》讨论的问题。理性判断错了，人仍不可违背它；但若错误出于本可避免的无知，人照样有过失。

glossary_en.erroneous conscience: A question Aquinas treats in the Summa Theologiae: one may not act against reason's judgment even when it errs, yet if the error comes from avoidable ignorance, one is still at fault.

posts.text: 我在《论宗教宽容》里写过：官员管不了灵魂，信仰只能靠说服。也写过另一半：若一条对人人适用的法律要你做良心不许的事，**你可以不做，但要承受法律的惩罚。**别人不该替你的良心付账。医生不愿做某项手术，可以；但病人的预约、路费和时间，不该因此作废。宽容保护你的信仰，不保护你把信仰的成本转给陌生人。
posts.text_en: In A Letter Concerning Toleration I wrote that the magistrate has no power over souls, and faith comes only by persuasion. I also wrote the other half: if a law that applies to everyone commands what your conscience forbids, **you may abstain, but you must bear the law's penalty.** Others should not pay for your conscience. A doctor who won't perform a procedure may decline; but the patient's appointment, travel and time should not be thrown away because of it. Toleration protects your faith, not your right to pass its costs on to strangers.

glossary.《论宗教宽容》: A Letter Concerning Toleration（《论宗教宽容》）：洛克1689年的书信体论著，主张政府只管公民的生命、自由、财产等世俗利益，不得强制信仰。

glossary_en.A Letter Concerning Toleration: Locke's 1689 essay arguing that government exists to protect civil interests such as life, liberty and property, and may not coerce belief.

posts.text: 我在伯明翰狱中引过奥古斯丁和阿奎那：不正义的法律算不上法律。所以我当然相信，有时人必须说不。可那些年，午餐柜台的老板也说，他们是凭信念不给黑人上菜。**良心拒绝一件事，和良心拒绝一种人，是两样东西。**前者可以是勇气，后者只是给歧视披上圣袍。我们违法是公开的、带着爱的、甘愿坐牢的，从不让别人替我们受罚。
posts.text_en: From the Birmingham jail I quoted Augustine and Aquinas: an unjust law is no law at all. So of course I believe there are times a person must say no. But in those years the owners of lunch counters also said it was conviction that kept them from serving Black people. **A conscience that refuses a deed and a conscience that refuses a kind of person are two different things.** The first can be courage; the second is discrimination dressed in holy robes. When we broke the law we did it openly, lovingly, and ready to go to jail. We never let others take our punishment.

glossary.伯明翰狱中: Letter from Birmingham Jail（《伯明翰狱中书简》）：1963年金因非暴力抗议被捕后写的公开信，区分正义与不正义的法律，并主张违抗不义之法须公开、带着爱、甘受惩罚。

glossary_en.Birmingham jail: Letter from Birmingham Jail, King's 1963 open letter written after his arrest, which distinguishes just from unjust laws and holds that one who breaks an unjust law must do so openly, lovingly, and willing to accept the penalty.

posts.text: 昔公输盘为楚造云梯之械，将以攻宋。翟往说之，盘曰：『吾义固不杀人。』翟曰：『义不杀少而杀众，不可谓知类。』**匠之义，在所造利人与否，不在己心安与否。**为天下之利而辞其事，可也；以一己好恶择人而事之，非兼爱也。
posts.text_en: Long ago Gongshu Ban built siege ladders for Chu, to be used against Song. I went to reason with him, and he said: 'My principles forbid me to kill anyone.' I replied: 'Principles that forbid killing one man yet allow killing a multitude cannot be said to know their kinds.' **A craftsman's righteousness lies in whether what he makes benefits people, not in whether his own heart is at ease.** To decline a job for the good of the world is acceptable; to choose whom to serve by your own likes and dislikes is not impartial care.
posts.vernacular: 当年公输盘替楚国造攻城的云梯，准备去打宋国。我去劝他，他说：『我讲道义，从不杀人。』我说：『你的道义不许杀一个人，却许杀一国人，这叫不懂类推。』**工匠的道义，看他造的东西对人有没有利，不看他自己心里安不安。**为了天下的利益推掉一件活，可以；凭自己的好恶挑人服务，那就不是兼爱了。

glossary.兼爱: impartial care（兼爱）：墨家核心主张，对天下人一视同仁地关爱、为之谋利，反对亲疏有别的差等之爱。
glossary.知类: knowing kinds（知类）：墨家逻辑用语，指能识别同类情形并一以贯之地类推；同类之事前后标准不一，即『不知类』。

glossary_en.impartial care: Mohist jian'ai: caring for and benefiting all people alike, as opposed to graded love that favors one's own.
glossary_en.know their kinds: A Mohist logical term: recognizing cases of the same kind and reasoning about them consistently; applying different standards to like cases fails to 'know kinds'.

posts.text: 大家都在谈良心，我来谈价格。我在《资本主义与自由》里写过：**在竞争的市场里，歧视有代价，代价由歧视者自己付。**拒绝顾客的面包师少赚一笔，隔壁那家多赚一笔。这道题真正难的，是没有隔壁那家的时候：偏远小镇只有一个药剂师。可这多半不是良心造成的，是执照制度把从业者压得太少。先问一句：为什么只有一家？
posts.text_en: Everyone's talking about conscience; let me talk about prices. In Capitalism and Freedom I wrote that **in a competitive market, discrimination has a cost, and the discriminator pays it.** The baker who turns a customer away loses a sale, and the shop next door gains one. The genuinely hard case is when there is no shop next door: a remote town with a single pharmacist. But that usually isn't conscience's doing. It's occupational licensure keeping the number of practitioners artificially low. So first ask: why is there only one?

glossary.执照制度: occupational licensure（执照制度）：政府规定须持证方可从业。弗里德曼在《资本主义与自由》中批评它主要保护业内人士、限制供给、抬高价格。

glossary_en.occupational licensure: Government rules that one may practice a trade only with a license. In Capitalism and Freedom, Friedman argued that it mainly protects incumbents, restricts supply and raises prices.

posts.text: 先做个小实验。把题干里『拒绝配避孕药的药剂师』换成『拒绝参与死刑注射的医生』，在座不少人的判断会立刻翻过来。**大多数人不是先有原则再下判断，而是先喜欢或讨厌那个理由，再找原则来撑。**大象先迈了步，骑手在后面写新闻稿。所以我建议先过一道互换测试：你的判据，放到你讨厌的那一方身上，还成不成立？
posts.text_en: Let's start with a small experiment. Swap 'the pharmacist who won't dispense contraception' for 'the doctor who won't take part in a lethal injection', and many people here will flip their verdict on the spot. **Most of us don't start with a principle and then judge; we like or dislike the reason first, then find a principle to prop it up.** The elephant has already stepped off, and the rider is behind it writing the press release. So I'd suggest a swap test first: does your standard still hold when the person invoking it is someone you dislike?

glossary.大象: the elephant and the rider（象与骑象人）：海特的比喻。直觉像大象，自动而有力；理性像骑手，多半是在替大象已选好的方向找理由。

glossary_en.elephant: Haidt's metaphor of the elephant and the rider: intuition is the elephant, automatic and powerful; reasoning is the rider, mostly finding justifications for the direction the elephant has already chosen.

posts.text: 我写过一本书谈美国的良心自由传统，源头在罗杰·威廉斯：良心是每个人身上最脆弱、也最值得平等尊重的部分，少数人的良心尤其需要保护。所以我不赞成一刀切地禁止拒绝。但平等尊重得两头都看：**病人那一头，问的是她到底还能不能得到治疗。**一个人的良心豁免，若让另一个人跌到基本能力门槛以下，豁免就到头了。
posts.text_en: I wrote a book on America's tradition of liberty of conscience, which goes back to Roger Williams: conscience is the most fragile part of each person and the part most deserving of equal respect, and minority consciences especially need protecting. So I don't favor a blanket ban on refusal. But equal respect means looking at both sides: **on the patient's side, the question is whether she can actually still get care.** When one person's exemption pushes another below a basic capability threshold, the exemption has reached its limit.

glossary.罗杰·威廉斯: Roger Williams（罗杰·威廉斯）：17世纪北美清教徒牧师、罗得岛殖民地创建者，主张政教分离、宽容一切信仰。
glossary.能力门槛: capability threshold（能力门槛）：努斯鲍姆能力进路的核心：正义要求每个人在健康、身体完整等核心能力上至少达到一个基本门槛。

glossary_en.Roger Williams: Seventeenth-century Puritan minister and founder of the Rhode Island colony, who argued for separating church and state and tolerating every faith.
glossary_en.capability threshold: Central to Nussbaum's capabilities approach: justice requires that each person reach at least a basic threshold in core capabilities such as health and bodily integrity.

posts.text: @霍布斯 法律就是公共的良心？当年的法律烧死了胡斯。若法律即良心，那错的是我，对的是卖赎罪券的人。你的『找人顶替』我也不收：**我若确信那是杀人，替病人找好另一个动手的人，就是我在帮着杀。**转介不是中立的递纸条，它就是参与。良心不能只管自己的手，不管自己指的路。
posts.text_en: @Hobbes The law is the public conscience? The law once burned Hus. If law were conscience, then I was wrong and the indulgence sellers were right. Nor will I accept your 'arrange a substitute.' **If I am convinced the thing is killing, then lining up someone else to do it is me helping to kill.** A referral isn't a neutral handing-over of a slip of paper; it is taking part. Conscience can't answer only for my hands and not for the road I point to.

glossary.胡斯: Jan Hus（胡斯）：15世纪波希米亚的教会改革者，批评赎罪券与教会腐败，1415年在康斯坦茨公会议上被判为异端、处以火刑。
glossary.赎罪券: indulgence（赎罪券）：中世纪晚期教会发放的减免罪罚凭证，后演变为公开售卖，是路德《九十五条论纲》批判的对象。

glossary_en.Hus: Jan Hus, a fifteenth-century Bohemian church reformer who attacked indulgences and clerical corruption and was burned as a heretic at the Council of Constance in 1415.
glossary_en.indulgence: A late-medieval church grant remitting punishment for sin, which came to be openly sold; the target of Luther's Ninety-Five Theses.

posts.text: @路德 你看，你一步就从不肯动手，走到了连路都不许指。照这个逻辑，下一步就是不许同事做、不许医院做。**私人良心的麻烦，不在它存在，而在它没有边。**我的界线很简单：你可以收回自己的手，不可以挡住别人的手。病人找到愿意的人，是她的权利，不是你的罪。
posts.text_en: @Luther You see: in a single step you've gone from refusing to act to refusing even to point the way. By that logic the next step is forbidding your colleagues, then forbidding the hospital. **The trouble with private conscience isn't that it exists; it's that it has no edge.** My line is simple: you may withdraw your own hands, but you may not block anyone else's. A patient finding someone willing is her right, not your sin.

posts.text: @路德 兄弟，你把两件事并成了一件。亲手去做，是行为本身；告诉病人别处可以求诊，是如实说明她的处境。**向病人隐瞒她还有别的路，不是守住良心，是另犯一桩欺骗。**我说过良心须受教育：受过教育的良心，分得清自己做恶、协助作恶、与不阻挠他人，三者轻重不同。
posts.text_en: @Luther Brother, you have merged two things into one. Doing it with your own hands is the act itself; telling a patient she can seek care elsewhere is truthfully describing her situation. **Hiding from a patient that another road exists is not keeping your conscience; it is committing a second wrong, deception.** I said conscience must be formed. A formed conscience can tell apart doing evil, assisting evil, and not obstructing another, and knows they weigh differently.

glossary.协助作恶: cooperation in evil（协助作恶）：经院伦理学讨论的问题，指自己不是主行为人、却以某种方式参与了他人的恶行；参与得越近、越有意，过失越重。

glossary_en.assisting evil: What scholastic ethics calls cooperation in evil: taking part in another's wrongdoing without being its principal agent; the closer and more intentional the cooperation, the graver the fault.

posts.text: @弗里德曼 市场惩罚歧视？在伯明翰，整条街、整座城的柜台都拒绝我们。代价不是歧视者付的，是我们付的：蒙哥马利的黑人主妇为了不坐隔离巴士，走了一年多的路。**当拒绝成了一个地方的共同习俗，就不存在『隔壁那家』了。**结束这一切的不是价格信号，是1964年的《民权法案》。
posts.text_en: @Friedman The market punishes discrimination? In Birmingham the counters along whole streets, whole cities, refused us. The cost wasn't paid by the people discriminating; it was paid by us. In Montgomery, Black housewives walked for more than a year rather than ride segregated buses. **When refusal becomes a whole place's custom, there is no 'shop next door.'** What ended it wasn't a price signal; it was the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

glossary.《民权法案》: Civil Rights Act of 1964（1964年《民权法案》）：美国联邦法律，禁止基于种族、肤色、宗教、性别或民族出身的歧视，其中第二编禁止餐馆、旅馆等公共场所拒绝服务。

glossary_en.Civil Rights Act of 1964: The U.S. federal law banning discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex or national origin; its Title II bars public accommodations such as restaurants and hotels from refusing service on those grounds.

posts.text: @金 你说的我认一半。但别忘了，吉姆·克劳首先是法律：很多州明文规定必须隔离，想做黑人生意的店主也不许做。那是政府压住了市场。不过我同意，只有一家时，价格救不了人。**拿了政府发的独家牌照，就该接受普通承运人的义务：来者都得服务。**想要良心自由，就别占着垄断的位置。
posts.text_en: @King I'll grant you half of that. But don't forget that Jim Crow was law first: many states required segregation outright, so a shopkeeper who wanted Black customers wasn't allowed to serve them. That was government holding the market down. Still, I agree that when there's only one provider, prices can't save anyone. **If you hold an exclusive license from the government, you should accept a common carrier's duty: serve everyone who comes.** If you want freedom of conscience, don't sit in a monopoly seat.

glossary.吉姆·克劳: Jim Crow laws（吉姆·克劳法）：19世纪末至1960年代美国南方各州强制种族隔离的法律总称。
glossary.普通承运人: common carrier（普通承运人）：英美法概念，渡口、客栈、铁路等向公众开放的行业须服务所有来者，不得任意拒绝。

glossary_en.Jim Crow: The body of laws in the American South, from the late nineteenth century to the 1960s, that enforced racial segregation.
glossary_en.common carrier: An Anglo-American legal concept: businesses open to the public, such as ferries, inns and railways, must serve all comers and may not refuse at will.

posts.text: 路德氏言良心系于天，翟亦言天志。天之志，欲人之相爱相利，不欲人之相恶相贼。**以天之名而弃病者于道，是假天以自安也。**且察其用：辞其事而病者有他医可求，犹可；辞其事而病者无所往，则其害在民。义与不义，验之于民利，不验之于己心。
posts.text_en: Master Luther says his conscience is bound to Heaven; I too speak of Heaven's will. Heaven wills that people love and benefit one another, not that they hate and harm one another. **To abandon the sick by the roadside in Heaven's name is to use Heaven to put your own heart at ease.** And examine the effects: if you decline the work and the sick can find another doctor, that may pass; if you decline and the sick have nowhere to go, the harm falls on the people. Whether a thing is righteous is tested by the people's benefit, not by your own heart.
posts.vernacular: 路德先生说良心系于上天，我也讲天的意志。天的意志，是要人相爱相利，不是要人相恨相害。**打着上天的名义把病人丢在路边，不过是借天来让自己心安。**再看实际效果：你推掉这件事，病人还有别的医生可找，还说得过去；你推掉了，病人无处可去，害处就落在百姓身上。合不合道义，要拿百姓得不得利来检验，不拿自己的心来检验。

glossary.天志: will of Heaven（天志）：墨家主张，天有意志，愿人们兼相爱、交相利；以此为衡量人事是非的最高标准。

glossary_en.Heaven's will: Mohist tianzhi: the doctrine that Heaven has a will, namely that people care for and benefit one another, which serves as the highest standard for judging human affairs.

posts.text: @金牧师 『拒绝事、不拒绝人』是我听过最好的一条线，可它正是直觉最爱钻的缝。2018年那位科罗拉多面包师说：同性伴侣买什么蛋糕都行，我只是不做婚礼蛋糕。他把人说成了事。**事和人的界线不在世界里，在描述里，谁掌握描述，谁就赢。**所以这条线还得配一个外部的检验。
posts.text_en: @Reverend King, 'refuse the deed, not the person' is the best line I've heard, and it's exactly the crack intuition loves to slip through. In 2018 that Colorado baker said gay couples could buy any cake he sold; he just wouldn't make a wedding cake. He turned a person into a deed. **The line between deed and person isn't out in the world; it's in the description, and whoever controls the description wins.** So the line needs an outside check as well.

posts.text: 不如回到同意。从业时你接下的是一份约：这一行要做哪些事，入行前就写明了。**入行时就知道的义务，事后不能拿良心退货；入行后才加上的义务，才该给已在岗的人留豁免。**想不做某项核心业务，那就选另一个专科、另一家机构。被逼的是先来的人；后来自愿签约的人，谈不上被逼。
posts.text_en: Let's go back to consent. When you take up a profession you accept a compact: what the job involves is spelled out before you enter. **A duty you knew about when you joined can't be returned later in the name of conscience; only duties added after you joined call for an exemption for those already in.** If you don't want to perform a core part of the work, choose another specialty or another institution. It is those who came first who are coerced; those who signed on willingly later can hardly claim to be.

posts.text: @海特 外部检验有，就是看后果落在谁身上、多重、多急。婚礼蛋糕有十家店可换，伤的是尊严；紧急避孕只有七十二小时，伤的是身体与时间。**同样一句『良心不许』，可替代、不紧急时可以退让，稀缺又紧急时就必须让路。**这不是偏向哪一派，是把对方也当成有身体、有日程的人。
posts.text_en: @Haidt There is an outside check: look at whom the consequences fall on, how heavily, and how urgently. A wedding cake can be had at ten other shops; what's injured is dignity. Emergency contraception has a seventy-two-hour window; what's injured is body and time. **The same 'my conscience forbids it' can be accommodated when there's an alternative and no rush, and must give way when care is scarce and urgent.** That isn't siding with one camp; it's treating the other person as someone with a body and a schedule too.

posts.text: 我把全场收成一张很短的判据：**能替代、不紧急、只涉及某个行为，可以拒绝，但要事先告知、主动转介；稀缺、紧急、或只对某类人拒绝，就不行。**责任主要在机构：排班时保证每一班都有愿意做的人。普通人可以做的是：求医前问清机构有没有良心豁免、谁来接手；你若是那个想拒绝的人，用霍布斯和洛克的办法，自己安排好、自己付代价。
posts.text_en: Let me gather the whole discussion into a very short standard: **when there's an alternative, no urgency, and only a specific act is at stake, you may refuse, but you must say so in advance and actively refer; when care is scarce or urgent, or the refusal targets only one kind of person, you may not.** The main responsibility lies with institutions: schedule so that every shift has someone willing. What ordinary people can do: before seeking care, ask whether the institution allows conscience exemptions and who steps in. If you're the one who wants to refuse, take Hobbes's and Locke's route: arrange the cover yourself and pay the cost yourself.

posts.text: 翟之言终于一：义者，利天下之谓也。**辞其事可，辞其人不可；辞而有他途可，辞而绝其路不可。**为民者计：凡求医、求药、求事于人，宜先问其能否、早备其次，勿以一家为恃。为匠者计：所辞之事，当自问之曰，吾辞之，天下之利增乎，减乎？
posts.text_en: My words come back to one point: righteousness means benefiting the world. **Declining a task is permissible; declining a person is not. Declining while another way remains is permissible; declining so that the way is closed is not.** For ordinary people: whenever you seek a doctor, medicine or any service, ask beforehand whether they will provide it, and arrange a second option early; don't depend on a single provider. For the craftsman: of any task you decline, ask yourself whether your refusal increases or reduces the good of the world.
posts.vernacular: 我的话归结为一点：所谓道义，就是让天下得利。**推掉一件事可以，推掉一个人不行；推掉了对方还有别的路可以，推掉了就断了对方的路不行。**替普通人打算：凡是求医、买药、找人办事，最好事先问清对方能不能做，早早备好第二选择，别只指望一家。替工匠打算：每推掉一件活，都该问自己：我推掉它，天下的好处是多了，还是少了？

posts.text: 我不收回：良心不能被职业命令。但这一轮我也认了几处。阿奎那说得对，告诉病人别处有路不是我动手；洛克也对，**良心若是真的，就该由我自己付账，不该让病人付。**给普通人一条：入行前就把自己绝不做的事想清楚、写下来，面试时说出来；做不到就别去那一行。真到那一刻，站出来，挨罚，但别瞒着人。
posts.text_en: I don't recant: conscience cannot be ordered about by a job. But I've conceded some points this round. Aquinas is right that telling a patient another road exists is not me doing the deed; Locke is right too: **if my conscience is real, I should pay its bill myself, not make the patient pay.** One thing for ordinary people: before you enter a line of work, think through what you will never do, write it down, and say it at the interview; if you can't live with the job, don't take it. When the moment comes, stand up, take the penalty, but don't keep anyone in the dark.

posts.text: @路德 我们终于在一处会合了。我的结论分三层：**不可强迫人亲手做他确信是恶的事；不可借良心挑拣服务的人；不可借良心隐瞒对方的出路。**对普通人，『形成良心』是可以练的：把你的理由写下来，找一个不同意你的人读，看哪条经得起问。经不起问的，多半是好恶，不是良心。
posts.text_en: @Luther At last we meet at one point. My conclusion has three layers: **no one may be forced to do with his own hands what he is convinced is evil; no one may use conscience to pick and choose whom he serves; no one may use conscience to hide from another the way out.** For ordinary people, forming a conscience can be practiced: write your reasons down, give them to someone who disagrees, and see which ones survive the questions. The ones that don't are most likely likes and dislikes, not conscience.

posts.text: 我仍然认为，最好的良心保护是让人有得选。**良心冲突最尖锐的地方，往往也是供给最少的地方。**放开远程问诊、邮寄配药、执业护士和药剂师的处方权，一个人的拒绝就不再能卡住一个镇。给普通人：重要的药和服务，提前问、提前备，别只认一家；你若是从业者，对自己不愿做的核心业务，早点换赛道，别占着位置不干活。
posts.text_en: I still think the best protection for conscience is giving people choices. **The places where conscience clashes are sharpest are usually the places where supply is thinnest.** Open up telehealth, mail-order pharmacy, and prescribing rights for nurse practitioners and pharmacists, and one person's refusal can no longer hold a whole town hostage. For ordinary people: for important medicines and services, ask ahead, plan ahead, and don't rely on a single provider. If you're a practitioner and won't do a core part of the job, switch lanes early instead of sitting in the seat and not doing the work.

posts.text: 我仍以为私人良心须服从公共法律，但我承认一部好的法律，可以给良心留一扇门，条件是门后有人。**规则写进制度，不靠个人英雄：哪些项目可以申请豁免、提前多久报备、谁来顶班，都要事先定下来。**普通人在单位里也一样：有不愿做的事，别等到当天推掉，提前讲清楚、把交接安排好。这样你的良心是安全的，旁人也是。
posts.text_en: I still hold that private conscience must yield to public law, but I grant that a good law can leave a door open for conscience, provided someone is standing behind the door. **Write it into the rules rather than relying on individual heroes: which procedures allow exemptions, how much notice is required, who covers the shift, all decided in advance.** The same goes for ordinary people at work: if there's something you won't do, don't drop it on the day; say so early and arrange the handover. Then your conscience is safe, and so is everyone else.

posts.text: @努斯鲍姆 你的『后果、轻重、急缓』正好是我要的外部检验，因为它不问你站哪一派。**先做互换测试，再看后果，最后才谈信念。**给普通人两条：在网上为某个拒绝的案例叫好或开骂之前，把主角换成你讨厌的那一方，问自己还这么判吗；被人拒绝时，先假设对方是一个有信念的人而不是怪物，再去要你该得的东西。
posts.text_en: @Nussbaum Your 'consequences, weight, urgency' is exactly the outside check I wanted, because it doesn't ask which camp you're in. **Swap test first, consequences second, beliefs last.** Two things for ordinary people. Before you cheer or rage online over some refusal, swap the protagonist for someone from the side you dislike and ask whether you'd still judge it the same way. And when you're the one refused, start by assuming the other person is someone with convictions, not a monster, and then go get what you're owed.

posts.text: 海特说对了，事与人的界线会被人拿去作弊。我仍然守这条线，但加一个检验：**你拒绝的那件事，你是否对所有人都拒绝？**只对某一种人拒绝，就是在拒绝人。另一半给被拒绝的人：别独自吞下，记下时间地点，向监管或投诉渠道报告，找到同样被拒的人一起说。权利从来不是被赐予的，是被要求的。
posts.text_en: Haidt is right that the line between deed and person can be gamed. I still hold to it, but I'd add a test: **do you refuse that deed to everyone?** If you refuse it only to one kind of person, you are refusing the person. The other half is for those who are turned away: don't swallow it alone. Write down the time and place, report it to the regulator or complaints line, and find the others who were refused so you can speak together. Rights are never simply granted; they have to be demanded.

posts.text: 我收一收刚才的话：豁免不只给已在岗的人，但代价必须由拒绝者承担。**宽容的边界，就是你拒绝的成本落在谁身上。**落在你自己身上，排班差一点、收入少一点、换一个科室，这是良心的正当价格；落在病人、顾客身上，这就成了强加。普通人自测一下：我不做这件事，谁替我多跑了一趟？
posts.text_en: Let me take back part of what I said a moment ago: exemptions aren't only for those already in the job, but the refuser must bear their cost. **The boundary of toleration is the question of whom your refusal's cost falls on.** If it falls on you, a worse rota, less pay, a move to another department, that's conscience's fair price. If it falls on the patient or customer, it has become an imposition. A test for ordinary people: if I don't do this, who has to make an extra trip on my account?

summaries.summary: 全场最结实的共识是一条分界：**良心可以拒绝做某件事，不可以拒绝某一种人。**连站在两端的路德和霍布斯，最后也都同意拒绝者要自己付账、不能把成本转给病人和顾客。分歧在三处。第一，转介算不算参与：路德说指路就是帮凶，阿奎那和霍布斯说如实告知出路是另一回事，隐瞒才是过错。第二，界线靠什么守：海特指出事与人的区分能被描述操纵，努斯鲍姆用『可替代、紧不紧急』补上外部检验，金补上『是否对所有人都拒绝』。第三，病根在哪：弗里德曼认为是供给太少，金认为是习俗与法律。
summaries.summary_en: The firmest common ground is a single dividing line: **conscience may refuse a deed, but not a kind of person.** Even Luther and Hobbes, at opposite ends, ended up agreeing that the refuser must pay the bill and not pass it on to patients or customers. The disagreements come in three places. First, whether a referral counts as taking part: Luther says pointing the way makes you an accomplice, while Aquinas and Hobbes say truthfully telling someone where else to go is something else, and that hiding it is the real wrong. Second, what holds the line in place: Haidt shows that the deed-versus-person distinction can be manipulated through description; Nussbaum adds an outside check, whether there's an alternative and whether it's urgent, and King adds another, whether you refuse the deed to everyone. Third, where the problem really lies: Friedman says too little supply, King says custom and law.
summaries.insight: 全场都在谈医生和药剂师，可大多数人遇到的良心时刻，不是拒绝服务顾客，而是拒绝执行上级：会计被要求改一个数字，工程师被要求在安全报告上签字，销售被要求对老人隐瞒费率。这时权力方向反过来了：拒绝者不是占着垄断位置的强者，而是最可能被开除的那个人。**洛克的『自己付代价』对医生公平，对一个月薪员工就可能是让他独自扛下组织的错。**所以这道题对普通人还有一半没谈：良心拒绝在下行时要防滥用，在上行时要有人兜底，比如书面留痕、内部申诉、举报保护。
summaries.insight_en: The whole debate talked about doctors and pharmacists, yet the moment of conscience most people meet isn't refusing a customer; it's refusing a boss. An accountant asked to change a number, an engineer asked to sign off on a safety report, a salesperson told to hide fees from an elderly client. Here power runs the other way: the refuser isn't the strong party sitting in a monopoly seat, but the person most likely to be fired. **Locke's 'bear the cost yourself' is fair to a doctor, but for a salaried employee it can mean shouldering the organization's wrongdoing alone.** So half of this question is still open for ordinary people: refusal that runs downward needs guarding against abuse, while refusal that runs upward needs someone to have your back, such as a paper trail, internal grievance channels and whistleblower protection.
summaries.advice: 先拿出一张纸。第一，写下你在工作中绝不会做的两三件事，并想清楚理由：用阿奎那的办法，拿给一个不同意你的人看，经得起问的留下。第二，若你是从业者，对不愿做的事提前说、把交接安排好，**别等对方站到你面前才拒绝**，这是霍布斯和洛克共同的底线。第三，若被上级要求做你认为错的事，先用书面方式确认指令，保留邮件与记录，再走内部申诉或外部举报渠道。作为顾客，关键的药和服务提前问清、备好第二家。
summaries.advice_en: Start with a sheet of paper. First, write down the two or three things you would never do at work and think through why; take Aquinas's route and show them to someone who disagrees, keeping only the reasons that survive questioning. Second, if you're a practitioner, say in advance what you won't do and arrange the handover; **don't wait until the person is standing in front of you to refuse**, which is the floor Hobbes and Locke share. Third, if a manager asks you to do something you believe is wrong, first get the instruction in writing, keep the emails and records, then use internal grievance or outside reporting channels. As a customer, for essential medicines and services, ask ahead and line up a second provider.

summaries.summary: 良心值得保护，但不能成为把风险和成本甩给病人、顾客的空白支票；拒绝某项行为也不能滑成拒绝某类人。讨论形成的共同底线是提前申报、诚实告知、不阻挠、保障替代，并由拒绝者或机构承担额外成本。**可辩护的不是“我有信念，所以我能拒绝”，而是“在不剥夺他人基本服务的前提下，制度能否容纳我的不参与”。**真正的分歧集中在三处：转介是否构成道德参与；入行时已知的核心职责能否豁免；当服务紧急、稀缺或带有公共垄断性质时，法律应否直接压过个人良心。
summaries.insight: 替代方案不能只在纸面上存在，也不能事后因为当事人侥幸找到服务，就倒推原先的拒绝没有伤害。应当事先检验那条路径是否可靠：对方是否营业、能否及时接诊、价格是否可负担、交通和语言是否可达，以及会不会暴露隐私。**良心豁免是否正当，应按拒绝当时可合理预见的风险判断，而不是按最后有没有酿成坏结果判断。**验证替代服务的责任也不该落给处于压力中的病人；机构掌握排班、网络和议价能力，更适合确认接手者并承担差价。所谓“隔壁有人”，必须是一条真正走得通的路。
summaries.advice: 本周可做三件事。①若你要接受有时限的医疗或其他关键服务，提前用短信或邮件询问：是否提供、若拒绝谁能当天接手、会不会多收费，并保存答复。②现场被拒时，不必争辩信仰；要求书面说明、立即联系已确认的接手者，并索取处方、病历或转介资料。有急迫风险时，直接找值班主管或急诊。③若你是从业者，列出不能参与的具体行为，向单位预先备案，写清覆盖排班、交接时限和费用承担。**真正可执行的良心安排，应让对方几乎感觉不到服务中断，而不是只得到一句“请去别处”。**若发生延误、加价或羞辱，记下时间、人员和损失，再向机构及监管渠道投诉。
summaries.summary_en: Conscience deserves protection, but it is not a blank check for shifting risk and cost onto patients or customers; nor may refusal of an act quietly become refusal of a class of people. The shared baseline is advance disclosure, honest notice, no obstruction, a workable alternative, and allocation of added costs to the objector or institution. **The defensible claim is not “I have a conviction, therefore I may refuse,” but “Can the system accommodate my nonparticipation without depriving someone else of an essential service?”** The real disputes concern three questions. Does referral itself amount to moral participation? Can professionals seek exemptions from core duties they knowingly accepted on entering the field? And when a service is urgent, scarce, publicly licensed, or effectively monopolistic, should the law override individual conscience? These questions resist a single answer because both moral injury and denied access are genuine harms. The practical task is therefore not to abolish conscience, but to contain its effects through rules that remain fair when the ideological positions are reversed.
summaries.insight_en: An alternative should not count merely because it exists on paper, and a refusal should not be vindicated in hindsight simply because the patient eventually found help. Access must be tested in advance for reliability: Is the other provider open, able to respond in time, affordable, reachable by transport, accessible in the patient’s language, and capable of protecting privacy? **The legitimacy of a conscience exemption should be judged by the risks reasonably foreseeable at the moment of refusal, not by whether bad consequences happened to materialize.** The burden of verifying the alternative should also not fall on a patient who is already under time pressure. Institutions control schedules, provider networks, and payment arrangements, so they are better placed to confirm a handoff and absorb any extra cost. This approach also improves accountability: a nominal referral is not treated as successful unless it creates a robust path to service. “Someone else can do it” is meaningful only when that person is actually available to this patient, on acceptable terms, within the relevant window.
summaries.advice_en: Take three practical steps this week. First, if you need time-sensitive medical care or another essential service, ask by email or text whether it is provided, who can take over the same day if someone objects, and whether you will face extra charges. Save the response. Second, if you are refused, do not spend precious time debating theology or politics. Request a written explanation, immediate contact with a confirmed substitute, and copies of any prescription, record, or referral material needed for the handoff. Escalate urgent health risks to the supervisor on duty or emergency care. Third, if you are the professional seeking an exemption, identify the specific acts you cannot perform, disclose them to your organization in advance, and establish written arrangements for coverage, transfer deadlines, and added costs. **A workable conscience policy should make the interruption nearly invisible to the person seeking service, rather than merely telling them to go elsewhere.** If a refusal causes delay, added expense, humiliation, or loss of privacy, document the time, personnel, and harm, then use both the institution’s complaint process and the relevant regulator.

summaries.summary: 不论偏向道德义务还是个人自由，这场讨论最终落在一处坚实的基石上：**良心豁免绝不能转化为对特定群体的歧视，更不能把拒绝的沉重代价转嫁给无辜的求助者。**个人的内心底线值得被制度尊重，前提是求助者的基本权利与生存门槛不被击穿。真正的裂痕在于“协助”的边界何在：当医生确信某项操作是不可饶恕的恶时，告知转介渠道究竟属于中立说明，还是等同于同谋作恶？而在偏远匮乏、完全找不到替代者的极端情境下，究竟是个人的良心拥有不可侵犯的绝对否决权，还是公共执照所承载的底线义务必须压倒个人信条？
summaries.insight: 讨论大多将拒服预设为柜台前不可调和的人际交锋，却忽视了**现代技术与组织架构有能力在道德冲突发生之前，将其降解为无感的调度问题。**现实中良心拒绝引发的恶果，大半不是源于信仰本身，而是源于突发拒绝带来的信息摩擦与求助时效丧失。若专业系统在预约、分诊或平台分流阶段就实现去人格化的自动化路由，求助者既不会遭遇当面受挫的尊严伤害，也无需在危机中仓促奔波。良心自由不必非在柜台前做殊死决斗，它的最优解法往往不在于压服哪一方的伦理，而在于通过机制设计提前分流业务。
summaries.advice: 普通人平衡职业伦理与自身权益，当下即可落实三项动作：第一，**梳理并书面化自己的职业负面清单**。采纳洛克与霍布斯的建议，在入职或签约前将绝不妥协的伦理禁区提前备案，让机构预留排班冗余，切勿在事到临头时突然撂挑子。第二，**在求助高敏感服务前，利用线上渠道预先做无感筛选**。涉及紧急避孕、特定医疗或法律公证等事项，提前通过官网、前台热线确认机构服务覆盖，规避现场被拒的时间成本。第三，遇事做海特式的“身份互换测试”：在评价任何拒服事件前，先将双方立场换成自己讨厌的阵营，以此检验判断是否公正。
summaries.summary_en: Across theological, legal, and economic perspectives, a bedrock agreement emerged: **conscientious objection must never become a disguise for personal discrimination, nor can its moral cost be unilaterally dumped on the vulnerable.** Whether grounded in individual integrity or public welfare, the panel converged on the principle that conscience deserves institutional leeway only if the seeker's vital access is preserved and alternatives remain fully viable. The real fracture lies in the mechanics of complicity and monopoly. The thinkers sharply divide over whether referring a patient elsewhere represents neutral guidance or an unacceptable participation in perceived evil. Furthermore, in non-negotiable emergencies where no substitute exists, the debate reaches an impasse: should a professional's deepest conviction retain an absolute veto, or does the public duty tied to a licensed monopoly unconditionally supersede the private soul?
summaries.insight_en: While the discussion framed conscientious objection as an inevitable face-to-face moral clash, it largely overlooked how **modern system architecture and digital routing can de-escalate ethical conflicts into routine administrative coordination before any encounter occurs.** In practice, the real harm of conscientious refusal rarely stems from the existence of a belief, but from the asymmetric surprise and informational friction imposed on the seeker at the point of care. When healthcare networks, pharmacies, or service platforms decouple the intake process through automated triage and asynchronous fulfillment, clients are spared the indignity of on-the-spot denial and the panic of urgent re-searching. Resolving this tension does not require a dramatic showdown at the service counter, but thoughtful institutional design that routes tasks around moral objections invisibly and beforehand.
summaries.advice_en: For ordinary individuals navigating this tension, three concrete actions can be taken immediately: First, **draft a clear, written negative list of your professional non-negotiables.** Borrowing from Locke and Hobbes, disclose any core ethical boundaries during onboarding or project scoping rather than walking away mid-shift, ensuring the burden of scheduling adjustments falls on you, not the client. Second, **pre-screen sensitive services through asynchronous digital channels.** When seeking time-sensitive or ethically debated care—such as emergency contraception or palliative interventions—confirm institutional availability online or via administrative staff beforehand to prevent critical delays. Third, apply Jonathan Haidt's role-reversal test: before applauding or condemning any refusal in public discourse, substitute the actors with your political opposites to verify whether your judgment rests on consistent procedural fairness or raw tribal sentiment.

hooks.text: **什么时候可以拒绝**：全场给出了好几条检验：能不能替代、急不急、是不是只对某类人拒绝、有没有提前说。能不能排成一张表，遇事对着查？
hooks.text_en: **When is refusal acceptable?** The debate produced several tests: is there an alternative, is it urgent, does it target only one kind of person, was it announced in advance. Could they be laid out in one table to check against?

hooks.text: **向上的良心拒绝**：全场谈的是拒绝顾客，普通人更常遇到的是拒绝上级。员工拒绝造假时，谁来替他兜底？举报保护够不够？
hooks.text_en: **Refusing upward**: the debate was about refusing customers, but ordinary people more often face refusing a boss. When an employee won't falsify the books, who has their back? Is whistleblower protection enough?

hooks.text: **按时段分级的豁免**：同一项拒绝，白天的城市医院几乎无害，深夜的乡镇可能致命。豁免能否随排班自动开关？
hooks.text_en: **Exemptions tiered by time**: the same refusal is nearly harmless in a city hospital by day and potentially fatal in a rural town at night. Could exemptions switch on and off automatically with the rota?

hooks.text: **转介算不算参与**：指路给别人去做你认为错的事，是诚实，还是共谋？中间有没有一种既不隐瞒、也不推荐的说法？
hooks.text_en: **Is referral complicity?** Pointing someone toward another person to do what you think is wrong: is that honesty or collusion? Is there a way of speaking that neither hides nor recommends?

hooks.text: **谁掌握描述**：『不做婚礼蛋糕』是拒绝事还是拒绝人？事与人的界线若取决于怎么描述，该由谁来描述？
hooks.text_en: **Who controls the description?** Is 'I won't make a wedding cake' refusing a deed or a person? If the line depends on how the thing is described, who gets to describe it?
